TOOLING BURST T4i-r1 — touch DEVICES always aim FORWARD (amends your T4i) (Run C-5; Matt 2026-09-16 bug report on the Vercel build: "All casting starts out behind the character and down.. depending on which way you end the tap on the cast button it will either cast down and left, middle or right, but never forward or up"; Matt rulings R-C5 Packet-84: no targeting protocol, CAST button stays, no tap-to-cast). task_id "T4i-r1". drax (web overlay owner) reports on the live web build: touch_controls.gd::_input calls get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() on EVERY InputEventScreenTouch, so keeper.gd _unhandled_input NEVER sees a touch on web; the aim falls through to get_global_mouse_position(), which on a phone is the browser-emulated mouse sitting on the CAST button. Your T4i bookkeeping (vfx_last_pointer_touch / mouse-motion-since-touch) therefore may never fire on the shipped build. Amend it so the rule no longer depends on seeing touch events at all.

Read ONLY, in this order:
1. /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst/SPEC.md — § 0, § 1, § 7 rows T4b (G1 component + targeting rule) and T4f (pierce / labels; "no targeting; CAST button stays; ranges unchanged").
2. /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst/BURST_RULES.md (the TOOLING row).
3. export/godot_import.py — the emitted keeper.gd (find the `_unhandled_input` handler that sets `vfx_cursor_override` on every InputEventScreenTouch, and `_cast_frame_changed` where `cursor` feeds `G1.resolve_target`), the G1 component script emission (`resolve_target`), tests/test_godot_import.py and tests/test_vfx_picker.py (extend only).
Do not read anything else. No web. No agents. No image generation. No pip install. stdlib only; Godot at /Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot for the headless import proof.

DIAGNOSIS (state it in out/files.json notes): on a touchscreen the last InputEventScreenTouch is the tap on the on-screen CAST button (drax's web overlay, bottom of the screen), so `vfx_cursor_override` = the button's world position = behind/below the follow-camera-centred Keeper; the cast resolves toward it. Mouse users never hit this because mouse events clear the override.

BUILD (minimal amendment of your T4i code in the emitted keeper.gd): the aim rule becomes device-based — if `DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available()` is true, EVERY player cast aims FORWARD along facing at the kit's range (no cursor, no touch point, no emulated mouse — Matt's ruling: no targeting on mobile; the CAST button casts forward); keep the probe hook `vfx_cursor_override` winning when non-null (tests/probes set it directly); on non-touch devices the mouse aim is byte-identical to the pre-T4i exporter. Remove the world-area-touch aim (it is unreachable on web and contradicts the no-targeting ruling); keep the TOUCH_OVERLAY_BAND constant exported for drax (harmless). Move the pointer bookkeeping, if any survives, from _unhandled_input to _input so a handled overlay touch is still observed — but the forward rule must not depend on it.
Tests (unittest, stdlib + the existing headless harness): the emitted keeper.gd contains the device-based branch; a headless probe with a stubbed touchscreen flag (expose a testable override such as `vfx_force_touch_device: bool` on the Keeper, default false, used only by tests/probes) casts with a mouse position deliberately placed behind the Keeper and asserts the resolved destination lies along the facing vector at range (±2 px); with the flag false the destination equals the pre-T4i mouse behaviour; the probe-override path still wins.
ACCEPTANCE (report in runs/C-5/t3/T4i-r1/acceptance.json): the two synthetic touch casts resolve as stated; the six kits + two burst kits export byte-identically except keeper.gd; headless import exit 0; FULL suite: `cd /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B tests/run_t0c.py` — all green except the five standing reds (test_f04_outside_at_least_three; three test_named_genuine_annuli_retained subtests; test_synthetic_contract_and_grid) plus the ten headless-Godot reds your sandbox produces (environment; the conductor re-runs outside) — name every red.

DO NOT touch: lane/, bible/, fixtures/, briefs/, SPEC.md, BURST_RULES.md, REGISTER_CARD.md, JUDGE_RUBRIC.md, MANIFEST.sha256, receipt.schema.json, transcribe.schema.json, oracle/, export/effect_kit.py, export/replay.py, any existing test except the two named (extend only), anything under runs/ except runs/C-5/t3/T4i-r1/. Do not run git. Temporary files ONLY under runs/C-5/t3/T4i-r1/. Write out/files.json listing every file you changed with sha256.
RETURN: the receipt (task_id "T4i-r1"): files = every changed path with sha256; images = 0 (INTEGER); calls_used; status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED with concerns listed honestly.
